1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, To the saints in Ephesus, and all y'all faithful in Christ Jesus:
1.2: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who done blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
1.4: Just like He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, so we could be holy and without blame before Him, all wrapped up in love,
1.5: Having predestined us to be adopted as His sons and daughters through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,
1.6: To the praise of the glory of His grace, by which He made us accepted in the Beloved.
1.7: In Him, we have redemption through His blood, forgiveness for all our mess-ups, according to the riches of His grace,
1.8: Which He made overflow toward us in all wisdom and understanding,
1.9: He revealed to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He set up in Himself,
1.10: That when the time is right, He's gon' gather up all things in Christ—everything, whether in heaven or on earth—everything's gonna come together in Him.
1.11: In Him, we also got an inheritance, predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things out according to His plan,
1.12: So we who first trusted in Christ would be for the praise of His glory.
1.13: In Him, you also trusted, after you heard the truth—the gospel of your salvation; and after you believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
1.14: Who is the guarantee of our inheritance, 'til we get what we was promised—redemption for the purchased possession, to the praise of His glory.
1.15: So after I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,
1.16: I don't stop thanking God for y'all, mentioning you in my prayers:
1.17: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation, so you can know Him better,
1.18: That your eyes be opened to see and understand the hope of His calling, the riches of His glory in the inheritance of the saints,
1.19: And the amazing greatness of His power towards us who believe, according to the working of His mighty power,
1.20: Which He showed in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
1.21: Far above all rulers, authorities, powers, and dominion, and above every name that's named, not just in this age, but in the one to come.
1.22: And He put everything under His feet, and gave Him to be the head over everything to the church,
1.23: Which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all things, everywhere.

2.1: And you, He made alive, when you were dead in your mess-ups and sins,
2.2: You used to walk just like everybody else, following the ways of the world, listening to that prince of the air, the spirit that's still working in those who disobey,
2.3: We all was wildin' too, living in the desires of our flesh, doing what we wanted in our minds, and we was children of wrath by nature, just like everyone else.
2.4: But God, who's rich in mercy, 'cause of His great love for us,
2.5: Even when we was dead in our sins, He made us alive with Christ (by grace, you've been saved),
2.6: And He raised us up together, seated us in heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
2.7: So that in the future, He could show off the greatness of His grace and kindness towards us in Christ Jesus.
2.8: For by grace, you've been saved through faith, and that ain't even your doing—it's God's gift,
2.9: Not by anything you did, so nobody can flex about it.
2.10: We are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared for us to walk in beforehand.
2.11: Remember that you, once Gentiles in the flesh—called "Uncircumcised" by those who got that circumcision done by hands—
2.12: At that time, you were outside, no Christ, no access to the promises of Israel, no hope, and no God in the world.
2.13: But now, in Christ Jesus, you who was once far away, He brought you near by His blood.
2.14: For He is our peace, who made both groups one, and broke down the wall that separated us,
2.15: He did away with that hostility, that law of commandments and rules, and made one new person from the two, making peace,
2.16: And He reconciled both of us to God through the cross, killing that hostility.
2.17: He came and preached peace to y'all who were far away and to those who were close.
2.18: For through Him, we both got access to the Father by the one Spirit.
2.19: So now, you ain't strangers or foreigners no more—you fellow citizens with the saints, members of God's household,
2.20: Built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ Himself as the chief cornerstone,
2.21: In Him, the whole building is fitted together and grows into a holy temple for the Lord,
2.22: And in Him, you also are being built together as a dwelling place for God in the Spirit.

3.1: For this reason, I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus for y'all Gentiles—
3.2: If you've heard of the grace of God that was given to me for you,
3.3: How He revealed to me the mystery, which I already wrote about briefly,
3.4: That when you read this, you can understand the knowledge I got about the mystery of Christ,
3.5: Which was hidden in other times, but now has been revealed by the Spirit to His holy apostles and prophets:
3.6: That the Gentiles are part of the same body, and they share in His promise in Christ through the gospel,
3.7: I became a minister of this mystery according to the grace of God that was given to me by His power.
3.8: To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given, so I could preach the unsearchable riches of Christ to the Gentiles,
3.9: And show everyone what the fellowship of this mystery is. It's been hidden from the beginning of time, in God, who created everything through Jesus Christ.
3.10: The point is that now, the wisdom of God might be shown through the church to the powers and rulers in the heavenly places,
3.11: According to the eternal plan He carried out in Christ Jesus, our Lord,
3.12: In Him, we got boldness and access with confidence through faith in Him.
3.13: So, don't get discouraged by my struggles for y'all—this suffering is your glory.
3.14: For this reason, I bow my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
3.15: From whom the whole family in heaven and on earth is named,
3.16: I pray that He may grant you, according to the riches of His glory, strength through His Spirit in your inner self,
3.17: So that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
3.18: May be able to understand, along with all the saints, the width, length, depth, and height—
3.19: To know the love of Christ, which is beyond understanding; that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
3.20: Now to Him who is able to do more than we could ever ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
3.21: To Him be the glory in the church through Christ Jesus, to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

4.1: So, I'm out here, a prisoner of the Lord, tellin' you: Walk worthy of that call you got,
4.2: With humility, gentleness, patience, and put up with each other in love,
4.3: Try to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
4.4: There's one body, one Spirit, just like you was called in one hope of your calling;
4.5: One Lord, one faith, one baptism;
4.6: One God and Father of all, who is above all, through all, and in all of us.
4.7: But to each one of us, grace was given, based on the measure of Christ's gift.
4.8: That's why He said: "When He ascended on high, He led captivity captive, And gave gifts to men."
4.9: Now, when it says "He ascended"—what does that mean, except that He first descended to the lower parts of the earth?
4.10: The One who descended is the same One who ascended far above all the heavens, so He could fill all things.
4.11: And He gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors, and some teachers,
4.12: For the equipping of the saints to do the work of ministry, to build up the body of Christ,
4.13: Until we all come to the unity of the faith and knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the fullness of Christ;
4.14: So we should stop acting like kids, tossed around by every new teaching, tricked by the lies and schemes of others,
4.15: But speak the truth in love, and grow up in every way into Christ, the head—
4.16: From whom the whole body, joined and held together by what every part supplies, does its job and builds up the body in love.
4.17: So here's what I'm sayin', and I'm testifying in the Lord: Stop living like the rest of the Gentiles, in the futility of their thinking,
4.18: They got their minds all darkened, separated from the life of God, because they ain't know the truth, their hearts are blinded,
4.19: They don't feel nothin' no more, so they gone off into all kinds of mess, living in greed and sin.
4.20: But that ain't how you learned Christ,
4.21: If you really heard Him and was taught by Him, 'cause the truth is in Jesus:
4.22: You gotta let go of your old ways, the old man, that corrupts you with lies and lust,
4.23: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
4.24: And put on the new man, created to be like God, in true righteousness and holiness.
4.25: So, stop the lying—"Let each one of you speak truth to your neighbor," 'cause we all part of the same body.
4.26: "Be angry, but don't sin"—don't let the sun go down while you're mad,
4.27: And don't give the devil a foothold.
4.28: If you used to steal, stop it—now work hard, doing good stuff with your hands, so you got something to give to someone in need.
4.29: Don't let no nasty talk come out your mouth, only speak what's gonna build people up and help 'em,
4.30: And don't grieve the Holy Spirit, the one who sealed you for the day of redemption.
4.31: Get rid of all bitterness, anger, rage, arguing, and bad-mouthing, along with all the hate,
4.32: Be kind to each other, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just like God forgave you in Christ.

5.1: So, be imitators of God, like dear children,
5.2: And walk in love, just like Christ loved us and gave Himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God that smells sweet.
5.3: But fornication, uncleanness, or greed? Don't even let that be named among you—it ain't right for saints,
5.4: No filthiness, foolish talk, or coarse jokes. That's not fitting—what's fitting is giving thanks.
5.5: You know this for sure: no fornicator, unclean person, or greedy man (who's basically an idol worshiper) has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
5.6: Don't let nobody fool you with empty words, 'cause because of that stuff, the wrath of God comes on the disobedient.
5.7: So, don't be part of that.
5.8: Y'all used to be in darkness, but now, you're light in the Lord. Walk like children of the light,
5.9: 'Cause the fruit of the Spirit is all about goodness, righteousness, and truth,
5.10: And finding out what's acceptable to the Lord.
5.11: Don't hang with the unfruitful works of darkness, expose them instead.
5.12: It's even shameful to talk about the stuff they do in secret,
5.13: But everything that's exposed is made visible by the light, 'cause whatever makes it visible is light.
5.14: That's why it says: "Wake up, you who sleep, Rise from the dead, And Christ will give you light."
5.15: So watch how you walk—don't walk like fools, but like wise people,
5.16: Make the most of your time, 'cause the days are evil.
5.17: Don't be unwise, understand what the will of the Lord is,
5.18: And don't be drunk with wine (that leads to wildness), but be filled with the Spirit,
5.19: Speak to each other in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
5.20: Always giving thanks for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
5.21: Submit to each other out of respect for God.
5.22: Wives, submit to your husbands as you do to the Lord,
5.23: 'Cause the husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church and the Savior of the body.
5.24: So just like the church is subject to Christ, let wives be to their husbands in everything.
5.25: Husbands, love your wives just like Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her,
5.26: To make her holy, cleansing her with the washing of water by the word,
5.27: So He can present her to Himself, a glorious church, with no spot, wrinkle, or anything wrong, but holy and without blemish.
5.28: So, husbands should love their wives like they love their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself.
5.29: Nobody ever hated their own body; they take care of it, just like the Lord takes care of the church.
5.30: We are members of His body, of His flesh, and of His bones.
5.31: "For this reason, a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh."
5.32: This is a great mystery, but I'm talking about Christ and the church.
5.33: So, let every one of you love your wife like you love yourself, and let the wife respect her husband.

6.1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, 'cause that's the right thing to do.
6.2: "Honor your father and mother," and that's the first commandment with a promise:
6.3: "That it may go well with you, and you may live long on the earth."
6.4: And you, fathers, don't provoke your children to anger, but raise them up in the training and teaching of the Lord.
6.5: Bondservants, be obedient to your masters according to the flesh, with fear and respect, doing it sincerely from the heart, like you're working for Christ,
6.6: Not just when people are watching, trying to please men, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart,
6.7: With good intentions, serving like you're serving the Lord, not people,
6.8: Knowing that whatever good anyone does, they'll get it back from the Lord, whether they're a slave or free.
6.9: And you, masters, treat your servants the same way, don't be threatening, 'cause you know your Master is in heaven, and He doesn't play favorites.
6.10: Finally, my people, be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.
6.11: Put on the full armor of God, so you can stand firm against the devil's tricks,
6.12: 'Cause our fight ain't with people—it's against principalities, powers, rulers of darkness in this world, and spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.
6.13: So, put on the full armor of God, so you can stand strong when the evil day comes, and when it's all said and done, you'll still be standing.
6.14: Stand firm, with your waist girded with truth, putting on the breastplate of righteousness,
6.15: And your feet shod with the readiness to spread the gospel of peace;
6.16: Above all, take the shield of faith, with which you can block all the fiery darts from the enemy,
6.17: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,
6.18: Always pray with all kinds of prayer and requests in the Spirit, stay alert with perseverance, and keep praying for all the saints,
6.19: And for me, that I might speak boldly about the gospel,
6.20: I'm in chains, but I'm still an ambassador, and I gotta speak boldly like I'm supposed to.
6.21: But so you know how I'm doing, Tychicus, my beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will let you know everything,
6.22: I sent him to you for that purpose, so you'll know how we're doing and he can comfort your hearts.
6.23: Peace to you, and love with faith, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
6.24: Grace be with everyone who loves our Lord Jesus Christ with a sincere heart. Amen.
